children.summary: This section outlines the restrictions on cash and intercompany funds transfers for JPMorgan Chase & Co. It details the regulatory requirements that impose limitations on the withdrawal and usage of certain cash and assets, including the need to maintain cash reserves at non-U.S. central banks. The section provides specific figures for restricted cash as of December 31 for 2022 and 2021, including amounts segregated for customer benefit and cash reserves. It also explains the limitations on lending between the Parent Company and its subsidiaries, including the conditions under which secured loans can be made and the caps on covered transactions. Additionally, it discusses the dividend payment restrictions imposed by regulatory authorities and the financial thresholds that must be met for such payments.

children.title: Note 27 - Regulatory capital
children.summary: This section outlines the regulatory capital requirements for JPMorgan Chase and its subsidiaries, as established by the Federal Reserve and the OCC, including Basel III standards. It details the minimum capital ratios required for CET1, Tier 1, and Total capital, as well as leverage ratios, and the consequences of failing to meet these requirements. The section also discusses the CECL regulatory capital transition, highlighting the phased-out capital benefits due to COVID-19 and its impact on capital metrics. Tables present the risk-based and leverage-based capital metrics for the years ending December 31, 2022, and 2021, demonstrating that the Firm was well-capitalized and compliant with all regulatory requirements during this period.

children.title: Note 28 - Off-balance sheet lending-related financial instruments, guarantees and other commitments
children.summary: This section details JPMorgan Chase's off-balance sheet lending-related financial instruments, including commitments and guarantees, which address customer financing needs. It outlines the maximum credit risk associated with these instruments, emphasizing that most commitments are not expected to be drawn upon. The section also discusses the allowance for credit losses related to these commitments and provides a summary of contractual amounts and carrying values for various lending-related instruments as of December 31, 2022, and 2021. Additionally, it explains the nature of guarantees under U.S. GAAP, including standby letters of credit and securities lending indemnifications, and describes the firm's risk management practices regarding these off-balance sheet arrangements.

children.title: Note 29 - Pledged assets and collateral
children.summary: This section details the Firm's pledged assets and collateral as of December 31 for the years 2022 and 2021. It outlines the purposes for which assets are pledged, including maintaining borrowing capacity and collateralizing various financial agreements. The total pledged assets amount to $793.2 billion in 2022, with significant components including investment securities, loans, and trading assets. Additionally, the section provides information on collateral accepted by the Firm, which can be sold or repledged, totaling $1,346.9 billion in 2022. The section also references related notes for further details on consolidated VIEs and securities financing activities.

children.title: Note 30 - Litigation
children.summary: As of December 31, 2022, JPMorgan Chase and its affiliates are involved in numerous legal proceedings, including civil litigations and regulatory investigations across various jurisdictions. The estimated range of reasonably possible losses from these proceedings is between $0 and $1.2 billion. Key cases include the 1MDB litigation in Malaysia, investigations related to the Amrapali Group in India, and various foreign exchange-related litigations. The section details ongoing litigation, including class actions and antitrust claims, and highlights the firm's approach to litigation reserves and the inherent uncertainties in predicting legal outcomes. Overall, the firm believes that these legal matters will not materially affect its financial condition, although potential reputational risks remain.

children.title: Note 31 - International operations
children.summary: This section provides a detailed breakdown of JPMorgan Chase's income statement and balance sheet information by major international geographic area, including Europe/Middle East/Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America/Caribbean for the years 2020 to 2022. It defines international operations as transactions involving clients outside the U.S. and notes that revenue and expenses are allocated based on client domicile and management location. The data includes revenue, expenses, income before tax, net income, and total assets for both international and North American operations. The majority of long-lived assets are located in the U.S., and the section emphasizes the integration of U.S. and international operations in financial reporting.

children.title: Note 32 - Business segments
children.summary: This section outlines JPMorgan Chase's four major business segments: Consumer & Community Banking, Corporate & Investment Bank, Commercial Banking, and Asset & Wealth Management, along with a Corporate segment. Each segment is defined by the products and services offered and the customer types served. Detailed descriptions of the services provided by each segment are included, such as banking, investment management, and lending. The section also presents segment results for the years 2020-2022, highlighting revenue, net income, and capital allocation methodologies, which are based on regulatory requirements and peer comparisons. Additionally, it discusses the managed basis of reporting, which adjusts for tax-exempt items to enhance comparability of revenue across years.

children.title: Note 33 - Parent company
children.summary: This section provides the Parent Company-only financial statements for JPMorgan Chase & Co., including statements of income, balance sheets, and cash flows for the years ended December 31 from 2020 to 2022. Key figures include income from dividends, interest income, and total expenses, highlighting a net income of $37.676 billion in 2022. The balance sheet details total assets of $555.687 billion and total liabilities of $263.355 billion as of December 31, 2022. Additionally, the cash flow statement outlines net cash provided by operating activities and significant changes in financing activities, including dividends paid and borrowings. The section also notes intercompany transactions and tax payments made by the Parent Company on behalf of subsidiaries.

children.title: Supplementary Information: Distribution of assets, liabilities and stockholders' equity; interest rates and interest differentials
children.summary: This section analyzes the distribution of assets, liabilities, and stockholders' equity, focusing on interest rates and net interest income for U.S. and non-U.S. operations from 2020 to 2022. It highlights the differences in interest rates, with U.S. loans yielding higher returns compared to non-U.S. loans, and discusses the significant portion of financial activities occurring outside the U.S. Additionally, it examines changes in net interest income, attributing variations to volume and rate for interest-earning assets and liabilities, and includes a detailed breakdown of net changes for 2022 versus 2021 and 2021 versus 2020. The section emphasizes the complexity of isolating changes due to volume or rate and the impact of market rate changes on interest income and expenses.

children.title: Interest rates and interest differential analysis of net interest income – U.S. and non-U.S.
children.summary: This section provides a detailed analysis of interest rates and net interest income for U.S. and non-U.S. operations from 2020 to 2022. It includes a breakdown of average balances, interest earned, and rates for various categories of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. Key figures highlight the differences in interest rates between U.S. and non-U.S. operations, with U.S. loans yielding higher interest compared to non-U.S. loans. The section also discusses the percentage of total assets and liabilities attributable to non-U.S. operations, indicating a significant portion of the company's financial activities occur outside the U.S. Readers can learn about the impact of geographic location on interest income and the overall financial performance of the company.

children.title: Changes in net interest income, volume and rate analysis
children.summary: This section provides a detailed analysis of changes in net interest income, attributing variations to volume and rate for interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. It includes a table that breaks down the net changes for the years 2022 versus 2021 and 2021 versus 2020, highlighting specific figures for various categories such as deposits, loans, and securities. The analysis emphasizes the complexity of isolating changes due to volume or rate, noting that when changes cannot be distinctly attributed, they are allocated to volume. Additionally, it discusses the impact of market rate changes and product composition on interest income and expenses.

children.title: Glossary of Terms and Acronyms
children.summary: The Glossary of Terms and Acronyms section provides definitions for key financial terms and acronyms relevant to JPMorgan Chase's operations and reporting. Readers can learn about various financial instruments such as asset-backed securities (ABS), credit default swaps (CDS), and mortgage-backed securities (MBS). It also explains important concepts like amortized cost, client assets, and risk management terms such as credit valuation adjustment (CVA) and liquidity coverage ratio (LCR). This section serves as a reference for understanding the terminology used throughout the 2022 Form 10-K report.

children.title: Signatures
children.summary: This section contains the signatures of key executives and directors of JPMorgan Chase & Co. as required by the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It includes the signature of James Dimon, the Chairman and CEO, along with other directors and officers, confirming their authorization of the report. The section specifies the roles of each signatory, such as Principal Executive Officer and Principal Financial Officer, and the date of signing, February 21, 2023. It emphasizes that JPMorgan Chase & Co. does not use a power of attorney for signing on behalf of any director.

children.title: Exhibit 4.6
children.summary: Exhibit 4.6 provides a detailed description of the securities of JPMorgan Chase & Co. registered under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, including common stock and various series of preferred stock. It outlines the rights and privileges associated with common stock, such as voting rights, dividend entitlements, and liquidation preferences. The section also details the characteristics of the Listed Preferred Stock, including dividend rights, ranking in liquidation, and redemption conditions. Additionally, it explains the role of Computershare Inc. as the transfer agent and registrar for these securities, and the implications of non-payment of dividends on voting rights and redemption capabilities.

children.title: Exhibit 10.18
children.summary: Exhibit 10.18 details the terms and conditions of Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) and Performance Share Unit (PSU) awards granted by JPMorgan Chase on January 17, 2023, under its Long-Term Incentive Plan. It covers the purpose of these awards to align employee performance with shareholder interests, vesting periods, and conditions for continued vesting, including job elimination and disability. The sections also outline obligations for confidentiality, non-solicitation, and compliance, as well as provisions for potential cancellation of awards based on performance metrics and adherence to firm policies. Additionally, it addresses recoupment policies for bonuses and shares in cases of detrimental conduct or failure to meet performance standards.

children.title: JPMorgan Chase LTIP Terms & Conditions of January 17, 2023 RSU Award Operating Committee
children.summary: This section outlines the terms and conditions of the Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) award granted by JPMorgan Chase on January 17, 2023, under its Long-Term Incentive Plan. It details the purpose of the award, which is to motivate employee performance and align interests with shareholders, and specifies the vesting period and conditions for continued vesting, including scenarios like job elimination and disability. The section also addresses the potential cancellation of RSUs based on performance metrics and compliance with the firm's policies, including a Bonus Recoupment Policy. Additionally, it includes obligations for employees regarding confidentiality, non-solicitation, and cooperation, as well as administrative provisions related to tax withholding and the binding nature of the agreement.

children.title: JPMorgan Chase LTIP Terms & Conditions of January 17, 2023 RSU Award UK Operating Committee
children.summary: This section outlines the terms and conditions of the Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) award granted to members of the JPMorgan Chase UK Operating Committee on January 17, 2023. It details the purpose of the award, which is to incentivize performance and align interests with shareholders, and specifies that RSUs are non-transferable and do not earn dividend equivalents. The vesting period is defined, along with conditions under which RSUs may be canceled or continue to vest after employment termination, including criteria for job elimination, full career eligibility, government office, and disability. Additionally, it includes obligations for recipients regarding non-solicitation, confidentiality, and compliance, as well as provisions for potential recoupment of bonuses and shares under certain circumstances, such as detrimental conduct or failure to meet performance metrics.

children.title: JPMorgan Chase LTIP Terms & Conditions of January 17, 2023 PSU Award Operating Commitee
children.summary: This section outlines the terms and conditions for the Performance Share Unit (PSU) award granted under JPMorgan Chase's Long-Term Incentive Plan. Key topics include the purpose of the award, which is to align employee interests with those of shareholders, and the calculation of the number of PSUs that will vest based on performance metrics. It details the holding requirements for vested shares, the impact of capital ratio performance thresholds, and the conditions under which PSUs may be canceled or adjusted. Additionally, it specifies the circumstances under which continued vesting is allowed after employment termination, including job elimination and disability, as well as obligations related to confidentiality and non-solicitation. The section also addresses the potential for recoupment of bonuses and shares in cases of detrimental conduct or failure to comply with the terms.

children.title: JPMorgan Chase LTIP Terms & Conditions of January 17, 2023 PSU Award Operating Committee
children.summary: This section outlines the terms and conditions of the Performance Share Unit (PSU) award granted under JPMorgan Chase's Long-Term Incentive Plan. Key topics include the purpose of the award, which is to align employee interests with those of shareholders, and the calculation of PSUs based on performance metrics and qualitative assessments. It details the vesting conditions, including protection-based provisions that allow for cancellation of PSUs based on performance and capital ratio thresholds. Additionally, it covers the implications of employment termination on vesting, the obligations of the award recipient, and the policies regarding recoupment and clawback of bonuses. The section emphasizes the importance of sustained performance and compliance with the firm's standards to retain the awarded shares.

children.title: Exhibit 21
children.summary: Exhibit 21 provides a comprehensive list of significant legal entity subsidiaries of JPMorgan Chase & Co. as of December 31, 2022, in compliance with SEC regulations. It includes subsidiaries organized in various countries, such as the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom, Germany, and India. The exhibit also notes that certain subsidiaries designated as material legal entities for resolution planning under the Dodd-Frank Act are included, even if they do not meet the SEC's definition of significant subsidiaries. This section is essential for understanding the corporate structure and regulatory compliance of JPMorgan Chase & Co.

children.title: Exhibit 22.2
children.summary: This section details the guarantee provided by JPMorgan Chase & Co. for the Global Medium-Term Notes issued by its subsidiary, JPMorgan Chase Financial Company LLC. It specifies that these notes are fully and unconditionally guaranteed by JPMorgan Chase & Co. and are issued under an Indenture dated February 19, 2016. The notes are offered under a Registration Statement on Form S-3, which was declared effective on April 8, 2020. Readers can learn about the structure of the securities, the role of the guarantor, and the regulatory framework governing these issuances.

children.title: Exhibit 23
children.summary: Exhibit 23 contains the consent of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, to incorporate their report by reference in various Registration Statements for JPMorgan Chase & Co. This report, dated February 21, 2023, pertains to the financial statements and the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting. The section lists multiple Form S-3 and Form S-8 registration numbers, indicating the scope of the consent. This document is essential for compliance with regulatory requirements regarding financial disclosures.

children.title: Exhibit 31.1
children.summary: Exhibit 31.1 contains a certification by James Dimon, the Chairman and CEO of JPMorgan Chase & Co., affirming the integrity of the Annual Report on Form 10-K. Dimon certifies that the report is free from material misstatements and accurately reflects the company's financial condition and results of operations. He outlines responsibilities regarding the establishment and maintenance of disclosure controls and internal controls over financial reporting. The certification also includes an evaluation of the effectiveness of these controls and disclosures of any significant deficiencies or fraud related to financial reporting.

children.title: Exhibit 31.2
children.summary: Exhibit 31.2 contains a certification by Jeremy Barnum, the Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of JPMorgan Chase & Co., regarding the accuracy and completeness of the Annual Report on Form 10-K. It affirms that the report does not contain misleading statements and that the financial statements fairly present the company's financial condition and results. The section outlines the responsibilities for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting, including evaluations of their effectiveness. Additionally, it addresses any significant deficiencies or fraud related to internal controls that could impact financial reporting.

children.title: Exhibit 32
children.summary: Exhibit 32 contains a certification by JPMorgan Chase & Co. officers, including CEO James Dimon and CFO Jeremy Barnum, affirming compliance with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. The certification states that the Annual Report on Form 10-K for the period ending December 31, 2022, meets the requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It also asserts that the report accurately reflects the company's financial condition and operational results. This document is significant for regulatory compliance and corporate governance, ensuring accountability in financial reporting.
